passage:
Eshaan's elbow swept through Hrithik's block tower and it clattered across the mat. Hrithik's face folded. From the sofa, Darshan said, "Eshaan. Say sorry. Right now." Eshaan looked at his shoes. "Sorry," he mumbled, flat as a coin, and Hrithik turned away with his arms crossed. Nothing had been mended.

Darshan came over and sat on the mat. He remembered how, only last night, he had said sorry to Eshaan for snapping at bath time, and had told him why he was sorry. "What could make Hrithik feel a bit better?" he asked quietly. Eshaan thought hard. "I could build it up again." "Ask him if he wants that," said Darshan.

"Can I build it again with you?" Eshaan asked. Hrithik sniffed, nodded, and held out the biggest block. Eshaan offered a hug, checking "Okay?" first, and Hrithik allowed it. Within minutes both boys were on the mat, arguing happily over whether the tower needed a flag, and the fall was forgotten.

qa.a: He knocked over Hrithik's block tower.

qa.q: Why did the ordered "say sorry" fail while rebuilding the tower worked?
qa.a: The ordered sorry came out flat as a coin and left Hrithik turned away with nothing mended. When Darshan asked what could make Hrithik feel better, Eshaan chose to build the tower again and offered a hug, Hrithik accepted, and both were playing within minutes.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling after the mumbled sorry?
qa.a: He was still hurt and unconvinced, and he turned away with his arms crossed because nothing had been fixed.

qa.q: How could Darshan keep teaching Eshaan what an apology means?
qa.a: By saying sorry himself and explaining why, as he did after bath time, and by asking what would help the friend feel better.

grounding: Shows the middle and end of an apology cycle: a forced sorry with no feeling, a concrete repair action, and friendship resuming quickly.
